blocks.x: Trigonometry A branch of mathematics that deals with the relationship between angles and sides of triangles. The trigonometric functions relate the angles of a right-angled triangle to ratios of the lengths of its sides/edges.

Trigonometric ratios Ratios between the edges of a right-angled triangle. These ratios depend only on one acute angle of the triangle, since any two right-angled triangles with the same acute angles are similar — so they define functions of that angle.
Sign convention Angles in trigonometry are measured anticlockwise. Angles measured anticlockwise are positive; angles measured clockwise are negative.
Angle θ→ Right triangle O, A, H→ Ratio (sin, cos, tan)→ Identity / Equation→ Truth set
Angles are measured anticlockwise from 0° on the positive horizontal axis. Each quadrant has one letter naming which ratios are positive there.
Only sine is positive; angle read as 180° − θ.
Only tangent is positive; angle read as θ − 180°.
Only cosine is positive; angle read as 360° − θ.

blocks.x: Finding a missing ratio with Pythagoras’ theorem
Given that sinA = 8/17 and that A is an obtuse angle, find cosA and tanA.

items: 1Write sinA as O/H.sinA = O/H = 8/17
2Use Pythagoras’ theorem H² = O² + A² to find the adjacent side.A = √(H² − O²) = √(17² − 8²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15
3Since A is obtuse (2nd quadrant, only sine positive), cosine and tangent take negative values.cosA = −15/17 tanA = −8/15

blocks.x: Find, without using tables, the values of cosθ and tanθ, if sinθ = 5/13.

items: 1Write sinθ as O/H.sinθ = O/H = 5/13
2Use the Pythagorean theorem H² = O² + A² to find the adjacent side.A = √(H² − O²) = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12
3Form cosθ = A/H and tanθ = O/A.cosθ = 12/13 tanθ = 5/12

blocks.x: Reduce the equation to a quadratic in sinθ (or cosθ) using the double-angle identity, factorise, then read the truth set off the given interval.
Find the truth set of the equation 3cos2θ + sinθ = 1, for π ≤ θ ≤ 2π.

items: 1Replace cos2θ using cos2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 1 − sin²θ.3(cos²θ − sin²θ) + sinθ = 1 ⇒ 3(1 − 2sin²θ) + sinθ = 1
2Expand and collect terms.3 − 6sin²θ + sinθ = 1 ⇒ 6sin²θ − sinθ − 2 = 0
3Let sinθ = x, giving a quadratic in x.6x² − x − 2 = 0
4Split the middle term and factorise by grouping.6x² + 3x − 4x − 2 = 0 ⇒ 3x(2x + 1) − 2(2x + 1) = 0 ⇒ (3x − 2)(2x + 1) = 0
5Set each factor to zero and solve for x.3x − 2 = 0 or 2x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = 2/3 or x = −1/2
6Substitute back sinθ = x and solve for θ in 0°–360°.sinθ = 2/3 ⇒ θ = 42°, 138° | sinθ = −1/2 ⇒ θ = 210°, 330°
7Convert each solution to radians (θ°/180 × π) and apply the restriction π ≤ θ ≤ 2π.42°=7/30π, 138°=23/30π, 210°=7/6π, 330°=11/6π — only 7/6π and 11/6π lie in [π, 2π]
